AD_COLUMN.NAME: Default Value
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Length
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An indication of the column length as defined in the database.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Length indicates the length of a column as defined in the database.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Key Column

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The key column must also be display sequence 0 in the field definition and may be hidden.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Link to Parent Column
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: This column is a link to the parent table (e.g. header from lines) - incl. Association key columns
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Parent checkbox indicates if this column is a link to the parent table.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Mandatory checkbox indicates if the field is required for a record to be save to the database.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Used for Record ID
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The document number will be used as the record key
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Used for Record ID checkbox indicates if the document id will be used as the key to the record

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.DEFAULTVALUE: @SQL=SELECT C_DocType_ID from C_DocType WHERE C_DocType.DocBaseType='GLJ' AND AD_ISORGINCLUDED( @AD_Org_ID@, C_DocType.AD_Org_ID, @#AD_Client_ID@) <> '-1' ORDER BY C_DocType.isdefault DESC

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document Status
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The Document Status indicates the status of a document at this time.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Document Status indicates the status of a document at this time. To change the status of a document, use one of the buttons usually located at the bottom of the document window.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Printed checkbox indicates if this document or line will included when printing.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Posted
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An accounting status button that indicates if the transaction has already been posted to the general ledger or not.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: An accounting status button that indicates if the transaction has already been posted to the general ledger or not. When doing the accounting manually this button can be used to post or unpost the transaction from the general ledger by hand.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document Date
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The time listed on the document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Document Date indicates the date the document was generated. It may or may not be the same as the accounting date.
AD_COLUMN.DEFAULTVALUE: @SQL=SELECT COALESCE((SELECT ENDDATE FROM C_PERIOD WHERE C_PERIOD_ID = @C_PERIOD_ID@ and periodtype = 'A'),to_date(@HeaderDateDoc@)) FROM DUAL

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Accounting Date
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The date this transaction is recorded for in the general ledger.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The date this transaction is recorded on in the general ledger. This date also indicates which accounting period within the fiscal year this transaction will be part of.
AD_COLUMN.DEFAULTVALUE: @SQL=SELECT COALESCE((SELECT ENDDATE FROM C_PERIOD WHERE C_PERIOD_ID = @C_PERIOD_ID@ and periodtype = 'A'),to_date(@HeaderDateAcct@)) FROM DUAL

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Period
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A specified time period.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Period indicates an exclusive range of dates for a calendar.
AD_COLUMN.DEFAULTVALUE: @SQL= SELECT C_Period_ID FROM C_Period WHERE C_Year_ID IN (SELECT C_Year_ID FROM C_Year WHERE C_Calendar_ID =(SELECT C_Calendar_ID FROM AD_ORG WHERE AD_Client_ID= @AD_Client_ID@ AND AD_ORG_ID=(SELECT AD_ORG_GETCALENDAROWNER( @AD_Org_ID@ ) from dual))) AND to_date( COALESCE(@DateAcct@,@#Date@) ) BETWEEN StartDate AND EndDate AND PeriodType='S' AND exists (select 1 from c_periodcontrol where c_periodcontrol.c_period_id = c_period.c_period_id AND periodstatus = 'O')

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.HELP: A more descriptive identifier (that does need to be unique) of a record/document that is used as a default search option along with the search key (that is unique and mostly shorter). It is up to 60 characters in length.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Accounting Standard
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Accounting Standard identifies the account principles that this accounting schema will adhere to.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Accrual
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates if Accrual or Cash Based accounting will be used
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Accrual checkbox indicates if this accounting schema will use accrual based account or cash based accounting. The Accrual method recognizes revenue when the product or service is delivered. Cash based method recognizes income when then payment is received.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Costing Method
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates how costs will be calculated
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates how costs will be calculated (Standard, Average) for valuation and accounting purposes.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Currency

AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates the currency to be used when processing this document.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Automatic Period Control
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: If selected, the periods are automatically opened and closed
AD_COLUMN.HELP: In the Automatic Period Control, periods are opened and closed based on the current date. If the Manual alternative is activated, you have to open and close periods explicitly.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Period
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A specified time period.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Period indicates an exclusive range of dates for a calendar.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: History Days
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Number of days to be able to post in the past (based on system date)
AD_COLUMN.HELP: If Automatic Period Control is enabled, the current period is calculated based on the system date and you can always post to all days in the current period. History Days enable to post to previous periods. E.g. today is May 15th and History Days is set to 30, you can post back to April 15th

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Future Days
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Number of days to be able to post to a future date (based on system date)
AD_COLUMN.HELP: If Automatic Period Control is enabled, the current period is calculated based on the system date and you can always post to all days in the current period. Future Days enable to post to future periods. E.g. today is Apr 15th and Future Days is set to 30, you can post up to May 15th

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Sales Order Sub Type
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
The SO Sub Type indicates the type of sales order this document refers to. This field only appears when the Document Base Type is Sales Order. The selection made here will determine which documents will be generated when an order is processed and which documents must be generated manually or in batches.
The following outlines this process.
SO Sub Type of Standard Order will generate just the Order document when the order is processed.
The Delivery Note, Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Warehouse Order will generate the Order and Delivery Note.
The Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Credit Order will generate the Order, Delivery Note and Invoice.
The Reciept must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of POS (Point of Sale) will generate all document

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Invoice on Even Weeks

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Invoice Cut-Off Day
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Last day for including shipments
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Invoice Day Cut Off indicates the last day for shipments to be included in the current invoice schedule. For example, if the invoice schedule is defined for the first day of the month, the cut off day may be the 25th of the month. An shipment on the 24th of May would be included in the invoices sent on June 1st but a shipment on the 26th would be included in the invoices sent on July 1st.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Default Value
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Value Format

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document Status
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The Document Status indicates the status of a document at this time.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Document Status indicates the status of a document at this time. To change the status of a document, use one of the buttons usually located at the bottom of the document window.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document Action
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A means of changing the transaction status of the document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: You find the current status in the Document Status field. The options are listed in a popup

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Print
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A reference stating whether or not the document has been printed at any time in the past.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Printed checkbox indicates if this document or line will included when printing.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Print Discount
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An option to have any discount printed on the invoice.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Discount Printed Checkbox indicates if the discount will be printed on the document.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Process Now
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A request to process the respective document or task.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: When this field is set as 'Y' a process is being performed on this record.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Processed checkbox indicates that a document has been processed.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document Type
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A value defining what sequence and process setup are used to handle this document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Document Type determines document sequence and processing rules

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Transaction Document
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The specific document type which should be used for the document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Specifies document subtype (eg. POS Order, Return Material, etc.) that each document (such as Sales Invoice, Purchase Order, etc.). Various document subtypes usually differ on the consequences they have. You can convert document types (e.g. from Offer to Order). The conversion is then reflected in the current type.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Sales Order
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A unique and often automatically generated identifier for a sales order.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Unique identifier and a reference to a Sales Order originating from the document sequence defined for this document type.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Sales Representative
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The person in charge of a document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Indicates the sales representative responsible for the transaction that the document specifies . A valid sales representative is a business partner marked as an employee and a sales representative.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Invoice Date
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The time listed on the invoice.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Date Invoice indicates the date printed on the invoice.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Date printed

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Default Logic 2
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Default value hierarchy, separated by ;
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: List Price Surcharge Amount
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The List Price Surcharge Amount indicates the amount to be added to the price prior to multiplication.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: List Price Discount %
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Discount from list price as a percentage
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The List Price Discount Percentage indicates the percentage discount which will be subtracted from the base price. A negative amount indicates the percentage which will be added to the base price.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: List Price Rounding
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Rounding rule for final list price
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The List Price Rounding indicates how the final list price will be rounded.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Min. List Price Margin
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Minimum margin for a product
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The List Price Min Margin indicates the minimum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original list price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Max. List Price Margin
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Maximum margin for a product
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The List Price Max Margin indicates the maximum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original list price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Standard Base Price
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Net unit price before applying this promotion. In case multiple promotions are applied in cascade, this price is the one after applying all promotions with more priority than current one.
This field is populated in case the used price list does not include taxes.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Surcharge Standard Price Amount
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Amount added to a price as a surcharge

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Standard Price Discount %

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Standard Price Rounding indicates how the final Standard price will be rounded.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Min. Standard Price Margin
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Minimum margin allowed for a product
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Standard Price Min Margin indicates the minimum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original Standard price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Max. Standard Margin
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Maximum margin allowed for a product
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Standard Price Max Margin indicates the maximum margin for a product. The margin is calculated by subtracting the original Standard price from the newly calculated price. If this field contains 0.00 then it is ignored.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Product Type
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An important classification used to determine the accounting and management of a product.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are four types of products available. Item type can be used to configure any product such as raw materials or finished products ready to be sold. An item can be flagged as Socked or not, can be part of a production process and/or can be a bill of materials. Item type is the only one for which a cost type calculation can be configured. Service type can be used to configure consultancy, transport or insurance services. Service type can be purchased or sold but can not be stocked. A service can be a bill of materials. Finally Resource and Expense are product types which can be used to distinguish between different types of products which can be purchased or sold but make not sense to stock. Expense type can be used to configure travel expenses fto be used while reporting Employee Expenses. The fact of using a given product type does not mean a different accounting. All product types account same way while being purchased, stocked or sold. All of them use the ledger accounts defined in the Accounting tab of the Product window.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Invoice Grouping
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
For scheduled invoicing, break into different invoices if the related values are different. The value is used as a binary code with 15 digits: 1.-Order organization (AD_Org_ID) 2.-Order (C_Order_ID) 3.-Shipment (M_InOut_ID) 4.-Invoice location (BillTo_ID) 5.-Ship location (C_BPartner_Location_ID) 6.-Sales representative (SalesRep_ID) 7.-Payment rule (PaymentRule) 8.-Payment term (C_PaymentTerm_ID) 9.-Currency (C_Currency_ID) 10.-Campaign (C_Campaign_ID) 11.-Project (C_Project_ID) 12.-Activity (C_Activity_ID) 13.-Transaction organization (AD_OrgTrx_ID) 14.-User defined 1 (User1) 15.-User defined 2 (User2)
For example, if you want to create different invoices for each ship location for a customer, use the value "By ship location" (000010000000000)

AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A non-unique identifier for a record/document often used as a search tool.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: A more descriptive identifier (that does need to be unique) of a record/document that is used as a default search option along with the search key (that is unique and mostly shorter). It is up to 60 characters in length.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Sequence Number
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The order of records in a specified document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Sequence indicates the order of records

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Sales Transaction checkbox indicates if this item is a Sales Transaction.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Order Quantity

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The unit of measure being used for the request.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Alternative order UOM for the product.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Movement Quantity
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The number of items being moved from one location to another.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Movement Quantity indicates the quantity of a product that has been moved.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Component Cost
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Component Cost
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Defines the weighting factor used to allocate the total operation cost among the produced products (P+). When an operation generates more than one P+, the total cost is distributed proportionally according to this value. This field applies only to produced (P+) lines.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Empty Cells are Zero

When creating a production run, by running the "generating standards" process required input and output product quantities are automatically filled in as specified in the work requirement phases.

If this is checked, the quantities will not be filled in and will be set to zero.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Conversion Rate
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Defines the conversion between Quantity and Process Quantity
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Defines how many final products each run of a process plan produces. See the following formula to understand the relation between the three elements:
Process Quantity = Quantity x Conversion Rate

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The number of Process Units required to be produced.

To avoid the need for calculating the number of process plan runs, the system allows for entering this number and then automatically calculating the required process plan runs.

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: Recalculate tax when Order or Invoice is processed. Usually taxes are recalculated when the document they are associated to is processed, so if the amounts are manually edited it has any effect. If tax is checked as no recalculate, manually edited amounts will be directly applied.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: IBAN
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: International standard for identifying bank accounts across national borders
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Code that identifies uniquely one bank account, no matter the country it belongs to. It consists of a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, followed by two check digits, and up to thirty alphanumeric characters for the domestic bank account number, called the BBAN (Basic Bank Account Number). It is up to each country's national banking community to decide on the length of the BBAN for accounts in that country, but its length must be fixed for any given country.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Country

AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Country defines a Country. Each Country must be defined before it can be used in any document.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: IBAN Length
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The length of the IBAN code of a bank account is variable, depending on the country.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Then International Bank Account Number structure do not stablish a specific length: it depends on the country. This field will define the length of the IBAN codes for that country.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: IBAN Code
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Country Code asigned to a country in the IBAN structure.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Then International Bank Account Number structure stablish that the first two digits will belong to the country. This country code is the one associated to a country of the application in this field.

AD_COLUMN.DEFAULTVALUE: @SQL=SELECT FIN_Payment_Priority_ID FROM FIN_Payment_Priority WHERE AD_ISORGINCLUDED( (CASE WHEN @#AD_Org_ID@='0' THEN (SELECT ad_org_id FROM ad_org WHERE name = ( SELECT min(o.name) FROM ad_org o join ad_orgtype ot on (o.ad_orgtype_id=ot.ad_orgtype_id) join ad_role_orgaccess ra on (o.ad_org_id=ra.ad_org_id) join ad_role r on (ra.ad_role_id = r.ad_role_id) WHERE ot.istransactionsallowed = 'Y' and r.ad_role_id=@AD_Role_ID@)) ELSE @#AD_Org_ID@ END), AD_Org_ID, @#AD_Client_ID@) <> -1 AND Isdefault = 'Y' ORDER BY Priority

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Indicates whether the report is "Point in time" (needs to calculate an opening balance if it does not exist) or a "Periodic" report (in this case that calculation is not needed)
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Indicates whether the report is a "Point in Time" or a "Periodic" report.
A Point in Time report is obtained as of a given date, taking into account the whole historical financial movements; an example of point in time report is the Balance Sheet.
A periodic report is executed for a date range and it does not carry forward the balance of accounting movements previous to the range; an example of periodic report is the Income Statement.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Status

AD_COLUMN.HELP: Status for the debt payment
AD_COLUMN.SQLLOGIC: (SELECT CASE WHEN (max(pc.periodstatus) = min(pc.periodstatus) AND min(pc.periodstatus) = 'O') THEN 'O' WHEN (max(pc.periodstatus) = min(pc.periodstatus) AND min(pc.periodstatus) ='C') THEN 'C' WHEN (max(pc.periodstatus) = min(pc.periodstatus) AND min(pc.periodstatus) ='P') THEN 'P' WHEN (max(pc.periodstatus) = min(pc.periodstatus) AND min(pc.periodstatus) = 'N') THEN 'N' ELSE 'M' END FROM c_periodcontrol pc WHERE pc.c_period_id = c_period_id)

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_COLUMN.NAME: FIN_Payment_Priority_ID
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Sets the priority of the payment plans generated when processing the invoice or order.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: Sets the priority of the payment plans generated when processing the invoice or order. The distribution algorithm will be driven by this priority. The pending payments for order or payments will be displayed ordered by the payment priority first and then by the due date.
AD_COLUMN.DEFAULTVALUE: @SQL=SELECT FIN_Payment_Priority_ID FROM FIN_Payment_Priority WHERE AD_ISORGINCLUDED( (CASE WHEN @#AD_Org_ID@='0' THEN (SELECT ad_org_id FROM ad_org WHERE name = ( SELECT min(o.name) FROM ad_org o join ad_orgtype ot on (o.ad_orgtype_id=ot.ad_orgtype_id) join ad_role_orgaccess ra on (o.ad_org_id=ra.ad_org_id) join ad_role r on (ra.ad_role_id = r.ad_role_id) WHERE ot.istransactionsallowed = 'Y' and r.ad_role_id=@AD_Role_ID@)) ELSE @#AD_Org_ID@ END), AD_Org_ID, @#AD_Client_ID@) <> -1 AND Isdefault = 'Y' ORDER BY Priority

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Dependency Enforcement
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
The values it can contain are:
*Major Version (default). The compatible versions are all the minor version within the same major version. If "Last Version" is defined being a different major version than "From Version", "Last Version" defines the highest compatible minor version; if "Last Version" is in the same major version than "From Version" this value is not taken into account. It is the default value. *Minor Version. Defines a strict dependency to the exact minor version. In case no "Last Version" is set, "From Version" is the only compatible version. Other case the compatible versions are all between "From" and "Last Version" values. *None. "From Version" is the only field taken into account, there is no restriction on different major versions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: User Editable Enforcement
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Defines whether the enforcement can be overwritten by user
AD_COLUMN.HELP: When a dependency/inclusion is "User Editable Enforcement", the enforcement defined for that dependency can be overwritten at instance level.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Instance Enforcement
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: Instance specific dependency enforcement
AD_COLUMN.HELP: In case the dependency is set as "User Editable", this value overwrites the Instance Enforcement one.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Timeout
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: The timeout is the frequency (in seconds) which the ping for a cluster service is done.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The timeout is the frequency (in seconds) which the ping for a cluster service is done, i.e., it represents the amount of time that should pass for the cluster node in charge of a cluster service to reaffirm itself as the leader. It is also used as a reference for the rest of the nodes in the cluster to determine if the leader is no longer alive and therefore if a new node should be promoted as the leader of the cluster service. Please note that it will be required to restart all the nodes in the cluster if this value is changed in order to make the new value visible for the entire cluster.

A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Search Key
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_COLUMN.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. When processes are executed from a button in a window, by default, they inherit permissions granted to the window. So if the window is accessible it can be executed without the need of explicitly granting access for that role to the process.

AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. AD_COLUMN.NAME: Days Overdue
AD_COLUMN.SQLLOGIC: (SELECT (CASE WHEN to_number(trunc((case when max(ps.outstandingamt) = 0 then max(p.paymentdate) else now() end)) -trunc(min(ps.expecteddate))) > 0 THEN to_number(trunc((case when max(ps.outstandingamt) = 0 then max(p.paymentdate) else now() end)) -trunc(min(ps.expecteddate)))ELSE 0 END) FROM fin_payment_schedule ps LEFT JOIN fin_payment_scheduledetail psd ON ps.fin_payment_schedule_id = psd.fin_payment_schedule_invoice LEFT JOIN fin_payment_detail pd ON pd.fin_payment_detail_id = psd.fin_payment_detail_id LEFT JOIN fin_payment p ON p.fin_payment_id = pd.fin_payment_id WHERE ps.fin_payment_schedule_id = fin_payment_schedule_id)

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Active
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document Type
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: A value defining what sequence and process setup are used to handle this document.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The Document Type determines document sequence and processing rules

AD_COLUMN.NAME: Document No.
AD_COLUMN.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_COLUMN.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).
